chunks: [The Qur'an:] Indeed, Allah, Glorified is He, has not counseled anyone with a like this Qur'an,
for it is the strong rope of Allah and His trustworthy means, and in it is the springing forth of the heart, and the springs of knowledge, and there is no other gloss for the heart than it.
although those who remembered it have passed away, while those who forgot or pretended to have forgotten it have remained.
So when you see good, support it, and when you see evil, turn away from it,
for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to say: 'O son of Adam, do good and leave evil; then you will be a swift, straight-going one.'

key_terms.جَوَادٌ قَاصِدٌ: A swift, straight-going one (metaphor for correct conduct)
key_terms.حَبْلُ اللهِ: The strong rope of Allah (a metaphor for the Qur'an)
key_terms.رَبِيعُ الْقَلْبِ: The springing forth/blossoming of the heart

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual benefits of the Quran and the Prophetic advice on doing good?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) elevates the Qur'an as the 'firm rope' (Habl Allah) and the sole remedy for the heart's clarity, contrasting the active remembrance of the wise with the negligence of the masses. This passage underscores the practical application of divine guidance through the Prophetic maxim to 'do good and avoid evil,' framing it as the essence of being a 'steadfast traveler' (Jawwad Qasid) on the path to God.
